newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-SRI LANKA BOWL OUT NZ CHEAPLY ON 1ST DAY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA BOWL OUT NZ CHEAPLY ON 1ST DAY.

text.p: Young fast bowler Nuwan Zoysa and spinner Muttiah Muralitharan claimed three wickets apiece as Sri Lanka dismissed New Zealand for 222 on the first day of the second test on Friday.

Sri Lanka, needing a win to square the two-match series, tied down the home batsmen with a mixture of spin and swing. Only opener Blair Pocock mastered the bowling with his best test score of 85, patiently compiled over 286 minutes at the crease.
The tourists scored an early breakthrough when Bryan Young, fresh from an unbeaten 267 in New Zealand's first test win by an innings and 36 runs, was run out for just four.

Matt Horne was clean bowled by Zoysa off a loose shot, and captain Stephen Fleming fell to a sharp catch in the slips. When a Zoysa inswinger trapped Nathan Astle lbw for nought, New Zealand were 100 for four.
The spinners dominated the afternoon sessions, with Muralitharan extracting significant turn.
Chris Cairns was caught by captain Arjuna Ranatunga at silly mid-on from Kumar Dharmasena's bowling, and wicketkeeper Adam Parore departed for 25 to another run out.
Soon afterwards, Muralitharan ended Pocock's long innings by having him caught close on the off-side from bat and pad.
Teenaged spinner Daniel Vettori was deceived by Muralitharan, who clean bowled him for four, and Dipak Patel was caught in the deep as he tried to slog the same bowler.

Simon Doull hit a brisk 20 before holing out at mid-on as New Zealand were all out just eight minutes before the scheduled close. Extras provided the second biggest contribution to the innings, with 30.
Muralitharan picked up three for 43 while 18-year-old left-armer Zoysa finished with three for 47.
